answer: Each identity registers one pearl-marked thread for one plot, locking a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it drops to the nadir and the depth is filed. An auditor recomputes the depth from the bathymetry table, checking the serial; readings off by over 3%, reused serials, or one thread on two plots burn the bond. The first identity pays 42; the k-th pays 42+5(k-1), since plot leases rise with scarcity; the 1000th pays 5037 and 1000 fakes cost 2,539,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-thread ring fails: one thread, one serial, so reuse is caught. An honest agent pays 42 once, bond returned.
